correctness.rationale: The exact twelve-edge Wagner graph and both dihedral edge orbits are constructed and independently checked. Five exhaustive nonempty-face enumerations give face counts 105,84,20,83,21; a valid disjoint face matching yields respectively 49,40,8,39,9 pairs. All 244,189,28,185,31 directed Hasse covers are formed and full topological sorting proves each matching acyclic. Critical profiles are (one 0 and six 2), (one 0 and three 2), (one 0 and three 1), (one 0 and four 2), (one 0 and two 1), proving exactly the claimed integral CW wedge types by Forman. The inclusion wedge-of-circles to a simply-connected wedge-of-two-spheres is null, providing both cofibration splittings. Separately constructed chain complexes check mod 2,3,5,101 homology and all faces; finite-field homology does not alone certify the integral homotopy claim.

originality.rationale: Directly inspected arXiv:2608.30601v2 Definition 3, main results and Problem 26: independence and extendable-perfect-matching complexes are studied, whereas ordinary matching complexes of Möbius ladders are expressly proposed as another question. Barmak arXiv:1007.0418v1 supplies connectivity only; Bayer et al. arXiv:2411.04601v2 apply to outerplanar graphs and do not cover nonplanar Wagner. Indexed Wagner results concern total 3-cut complex or edge ideals; closest named Möbius-Kantor matching result uses a different 16-vertex graph. Exact aliases, line graph, possible stronger family coverage and stored prior scientific claims checked; no covering statement was identified. Unindexed equivalent work remains a real residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent calculation for this finite graph under nonstandard graph or complex names could occur in unindexed or unpublished literature; no claim of absolute priority follows from the searches.
The result is limited to this particular eight-vertex case and does not establish a periodic family formula.

value.rationale: Wagner is the canonical eight-vertex nonplanar Möbius ladder, making its ordinary matching-complex homotopy a directly motivated instance of arXiv:2608.30601v2 Problem 26. The simultaneous classification of two edge-orbit links and deletions gives two genuinely different null-attaching splittings of the same six-sphere wedge, rather than a raw face census or Euler-characteristic exercise. No general theorem is claimed beyond the finite graph.
